text: "Full Leather Jacket" is the 21st episode of the HBO original series The Sopranos and the eighth episode of the show's second season. It was written by Robin Green and Mitchell Burgess, directed by Allen Coulter, and originally aired on March 5, 2000. Meadow hopes to attend Berkeley, but her parents, Tony and Carmela, want to prevent it. Their neighbor, Jean Cusamano, has a sister, Joan O'Connell, who is a distinguished alumna of Georgetown University. Carmela persuades Jean to ask Joan to write a letter of recommendation for Meadow. Joan declines, but Carmela visits her, offers her a ricotta pie, and insists, "I want you to write that letter." Jean informs Carmela that the letter has been written, and Carmela requests a copy. Silvio and Paulie pressure Richie to build a wheelchair ramp for Beansie's house as partial reparation for crippling him. Richie refuses scornfully, but when he learns the request comes from Tony, he sends his nephew Vito Spatafore and his construction workers to fully adapt Beansie's house. Richie owns a leather jacket he obtained years ago from the feared mobster Rocco DiMeo. He gives it to Tony, who accepts it reluctantly but politely. Richie values the jacket and the act of giving it to Tony deeply. He is deeply offended when he sees it being worn by the husband of the Sopranos' maid. Adriana, embarrassed by Christopher in a restaurant, leaves him and returns to her mother's. Christopher goes to her, proposes marriage, and presents her with a ring. She says she loves him and the ring. In bed, he tells her, "I'm back on track, rededicating myself"—to her and to Tony. Matt and Sean continue working with Christopher, breaking into safes. After enduring various slights and snubs from members of the DiMeo family, they feel they are making no progress and decide to take drastic action. They ambush Christopher as he leaves a diner, believing this will earn them favor with Richie. Christopher is shot three times and left unconscious; Sean is killed. Matt flees and asks for Richie's protection; Richie, furious, chases him away. As Christopher lies comatose in the hospital, Tony asks, "How could this happen?" The episode's title is a play on the 1987 film Full Metal Jacket, whose title refers to full metal jacket bullets. Here, it alludes to the leather jacket that Richie gave to Tony. Additionally, after Christopher is shot, the camera pans the sidewalk showing the metal cartridge casings expelled from the weapons. Thematically, Matt and Sean ambushing Christopher to prove themselves to Richie reflects the killing of the Vietnamese sniper by Joker in the film Full Metal Jacket, which—on one level—can be seen as a reluctant act by Joker to prove himself to Animal Mother and the others. Richie is shown as being abusive of others around him in a manner similar to how Animal Mother abuses the other Lusthog Squad marines, who still rely on him for their safety. More generally, this episode is connected to the film referenced in its title through the theme of "loss of innocence."
